summary.en: Israel has built a 90km network of military roads in southern Lebanon, including one in the Shebaa Valley buffer zone, and opened new bases, while Hezbollah continues artillery fire on Israeli positions and has begun cash payments to war victims and displaced families. Israeli strikes have wounded a Lebanese footballer and led to the detention of a 65-year-old retired engineer. Protests against Israeli attacks on Palestine and Lebanon have taken place in Sweden. The United Nations reports 300,000 people displaced in Lebanon, and there were 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel har bygget et 90 km nettverk av militære veier i sørlige Libanon, inkludert en i bufferområdet i Shebaa-dalen, og åpnet nye baser, mens Hizbollah fortsetter artilleriskudd mot israelske posisjoner og har begynt med kontantutbetalinger til krigsofre og fordrevne familier. Israelske angrep har såret en libanesisk fotballspiller og ført til fengsling av en 65‑år gammel pensjonert ingeniør. Protester mot israelske angrep på Palestina og Libanon har funnet sted i Sverige. FN rapporterer at 300 000 personer er fordrevet i Libanon, og det var 4 335 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
